title: Pilot kickoff - retention, redaction & benchmark sizing sync
summary: Kickoff to scope pilot focused on prompt retention and redaction for a patient-facing triage assistant. Agreed on benchmark cases, initial workload sizing (burst vs steady TPS), redaction levels (field vs full prompt), and a 3-week pilot with two benchmark runs. Action items include sharing security docs, test dataset, and Redwood to propose benchmark script and tentative timeline.
next_steps: Redwood to send security pack & SOC2 + encryption notes (Avery)
Customer to share redacted sample prompts and 3 months of traffic histogram (Maya)
Diego to propose benchmark harness and SLOs by 2026-05-25
action_items: Avery: share security pack, KMS integration notes (due 2026-05-22)
Maya: provide sample prompts + traffic histograms (due 2026-05-24)
Diego: draft benchmark harness & test plan (due 2026-05-25)
Lena: give access requirements for private VPC pilot if needed (due 2026-05-27)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-20
Start time (UTC): 16:00
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Morales (Redwood SE), Sofia Li (Redwood SA), Maya Patel (Clearwater Product), Rashid Khan (Clearwater Data Privacy), Lena Ortiz (Clearwater SRE), Tom B. (CTO, joined 10m)

Summary: kickoff to scope a short pilot to validate prompt retention, redaction, and benchmark sizing for a patient triage assistant use-case. Customer wants clear SLOs for latency, cost per 1k tokens, and guarantees around prompt retention and PII removal.

00:00 - Avery: Okay, thanks everyone for hopping on. Quick intros — I'm Avery, AE here at Redwood, with Diego who will run the bench and Sofia on architecture. Maya, do you want to do a quick intro?
00:12 - Maya: Sure, hi all — Maya Patel, lead product for the triage assistant at Clearwater. We're trying to run a small pilot to make sure we can keep patient data out of logs, or at least redacted, and to size cost and latency for expected loads.
00:26 - Rashid: Rashid here, I look after privacy and compliance. Our big flags are prompt persistence, searchability, and retention windows. We need to know what's stored where and for how long, and how redaction works for free-text patient notes.
00:40 - Diego: Got it. High level: we usually support hosted and private — for this pilot are you planning to use Redwood hosted or Private VPC?
00:47 - Maya: Initially hosted to move quickly, but we need to validate that hosted can meet our retention and redaction controls. If not, we'll consider private.
00:55 - Sofia: Quick note — hosted can be configured with short retention windows and field-level redaction, but private gives more control for KMS/HSM and no cross-tenant logging. We'll map options.
01:05 - Tom B.: (pops on) Hi, sorry late. Two things: one, we need monthly audit logs for regulators; two, worst-case latency shouldn't exceed 450ms p50 for the most common flow.
01:18 - Avery: Noted. Diego, can you talk about benchmark approach?
01:22 - Diego: Yeah — for sizing we want steady-state and burst profiles. Can you share expected TPS and percentiles for sequence lengths? Even rough histograms help. For bench we typically run: small synthetic workload, then replay a redacted sample set, and measure latency p50/p95, tokens/sec, and cost per 1k tokens. We also test with KV/prefix caching to mimic chat flows.
01:45 - Maya: We have a median prompt length around 120 tokens, but some back-and-forth reach 800 tokens. TPS is low per user but concurrent peak ~40 requests/sec across the service during mornings.
01:56 - Rashid: For PII we would prefer automatic redaction at ingestion then store only a hashed reference. Can Redwood do redaction before anything hits persistent logs?
02:06 - Sofia: Short answer: yes, we have ingestion-time redaction hooks; we can either do pre-send client-side redaction (preferred by some customers) or server-side redaction that strips or masks PHI fields before storage. There is a tradeoff: full prompt redaction can reduce usefulness of telemetry and impact evaluation.
02:25 - Maya: That's my concern — if we mask too much we can't iterate on prompts. Maybe we can do field-level redaction and keep a metadata-only trace for debugging.
02:34 - Diego: We can keep token-preserving hashed placeholders for PII so model context remains but raw values aren't stored. That also helps reproducible benches.
02:45 - Rashid: I want to confirm encryption at rest with customer-managed keys. KMS integration?
02:49 - Avery: Redwood supports KMS and for Private we do HSM options; hosted can be configured with a customer KMS key (bring-your-own-key) in many regions. We'll include the KMS integration guide in the security pack.
03:02 - Tom B.: About audit logs — can you export full audit trail to our SIEM? We need immutable logs for a year.
03:08 - Sofia: Yep, we can stream audit logs to your S3 or Splunk; retention policy can be set on the export side. Internally we keep shorter retention but export satisfies regulation. We'll document the pipeline.
03:20 - Maya: Back to benchmarks — what's realistic for the pilot run length? We want two benchmark runs: baseline (no redaction) and production-like (ingestion redaction + caching). Each run should be 2-4 hours to gather stable p95 numbers. Is that doable?
03:36 - Diego: Yes — two runs over two weeks is typical. We'll also want to run edge-case long sequences to test KV cache performance.
03:44 - Rashid: Success criteria from our side: no PII persisted in logs, p95 latency < 900ms for long flows, p50 < 450ms for common flow, and cost estimate within 20% of target. Also must pass a basic redaction test set (we'll provide).
03:58 - Avery: Good concrete criteria. We'll add those as the POC acceptance checklist. Any blockers on timelines?
04:05 - Maya: Internal reviewers need security docs and a short implementation plan to greenlight. If we get docs by Friday, we can start data prep next week.
04:12 - Avery: We'll send the security pack (SOC2, ISO summary, KMS/HSM notes) by Friday. Diego will draft the bench harness and SLOs.
04:20 - Diego: For the harness I'll propose a reproducible script: replay of 10k sample prompts, with 1) raw prompts; 2) redacted prompts; measure latency, token throughput, failure-rate, and memory/kv miss rates. We also capture cost run-rate. Will include steps to replay at different concurrency to hit 40 RPS.
04:39 - Lena: From SRE perspective, we'd like to check connection lifecycle, TLS mutual auth, and IP allowlisting for hosted if we go that route. Also, how are secrets rotated?
04:49 - Sofia: We support mTLS and IP allowlists, and for secrets we rotate keys and can integrate with your vault. We'll include a short checklist for connection setup.
04:58 - Rashid: One more question — prompt storage retention: can we do a 7-day window for full prompt retention and then archive only hashed metadata for 1 year?
05:05 - Avery: Yes, retention windows are configurable; hosted can do short windows and a secondary hashed archive. We'll document the exact flows.
05:12 - Tom B.: I also want a quick note on fallback: if hosting latency jumps, can Redwood fall back to a smaller quantized model to maintain latency SLOs?
05:19 - Diego: We support model fallbacks — it's part of routing policies. For the bench we'll test a fallback scenario to measure quality drop and latency gains.
05:27 - Maya: Great. Last item — pricing expectations: we need a rough estimate for the pilot to budget.
05:33 - Avery: I'll send a pilot cost estimate based on tokens and expected concurrency — that'll be preliminary. If you need a firm number we'll scope dedicated capacity.
05:40 - Maya: Okay thanks everyone. Recap of action items?
05:44 - Avery: I'll send security pack and pilot cost ballpark by Friday; Diego sends bench plan by Monday-ish; Maya shares prompts & histograms; Lena shares connection constraints; we aim to run first bench week of June 1.
05:58 - Rashid: Thanks, will check with legal on export controls but proceed.
06:02 - Avery: Thanks all, we'll follow up in calendar with the bench run and a shared doc link.

Notes on transcription: occasional misheard tokens ("KMS" sometimes transcribed as "K BMS"), and speaker overlap near the end.

References shared: security_pack_v1.pdf (link to be sent), sample_prompt_schema.csv (customer to share), bench-harness-proposal.md (Redwood to send)

End of transcript.
